name: Stopping models from making things up
gist: Preventing models from confidently stating false information when they process images and text, checking against what they actually see.
explain: A model trained to describe images or answer questions about them sometimes generates output that sounds confident but is not grounded in reality. A model might say a person is holding a banana when they are holding an apple, or claim a chair is red when it is blue. It is making things up — hallucinating details that are not in the image. This happens because the model has learned to generate plausible-sounding text from its training data, but plausible-sounding does not mean true. A model trained on millions of images and captions has absorbed patterns and associations: if it sees a kitchen, it might generate 'there is a refrigerator' because fridges are common in kitchens, even if this particular kitchen image does not show one. The model is not trying to lie; it is just pattern-matching.

The problem is serious in practice because users trust AI systems to describe reality accurately, and they make decisions based on that trust. When an AI hallucinates, those decisions cause real harm. A doctor uses a multimodal AI to help interpret medical images, trusting it because it has high accuracy overall. The AI confidently claims 'this patient has a tumor' when the image actually shows no tumor. Based on this false claim, the doctor starts aggressive treatment: surgery, chemotherapy, radiation. These treatments damage the patient's healthy body and cause suffering, all based on the AI's hallucination. A person who is blind relies on an AI to describe images because they trust it to report what is there. The AI invents details: 'there is a red car in the parking lot' when the image shows empty space. Based on this false description, the person builds incorrect beliefs about the world. Hallucination happens because the model learns two separate things: how to perceive images (building a representation of what is in them) and how to generate text (learning language patterns). These two can drift apart — the text generation learns to fill in plausible details rather than staying faithful to the perception. Some hallucinations are clear (inventing objects that are not there), but some are subtle: a slight exaggeration of size, a misidentified color, a missing context that changes the meaning.

Research on reducing hallucination tackles the problem from several angles. Some work focuses on training methods: if you penalize the model when it generates text that is not supported by the visual content, it learns to be more faithful. Some approaches use constrained decoding — when the model is generating text, you check at each step whether the next word is justified by the image, and only allow words that are supported. This works because you stop the model before it makes something up by blocking implausible words at generation time. Others build models that explicitly reason about uncertainty — if the model is not sure about something, it should say so rather than guess. Some work trains models with special symbols (called tokens, which are one chunk of text the model reads) that mean 'I cannot see this clearly' or 'this is partially obscured.' Some focus on building better visual representations by using multiple levels of detail, so the model has both coarse and fine-grained information about what is in the image. And some work trains the model to explicitly cite which part of the image supports each claim in the description — if the model says 'there is a dog,' it should point to where the dog is.

papers.title: Correcting Visual Blur Induced by Attention Distraction to Reduce Hallucinations: Algorithm and Theory
papers.contribution: AFIP reduces hallucinations by addressing the underlying attention mechanism across multiple benchmarks and models.

papers.title: DEGAP: Dynamic Entropy-Guided Attention Perturbation for Contrastive Decoding in Large Vision-Language Models
papers.contribution: Effectively mitigate various hallucination types across seven benchmarks while maintaining strong general VQA performance.

papers.title: Mitigating Hallucinations in Large Vision-Language Models via Causal Route Gating
papers.contribution: Consistently reduces hallucination-related errors across five benchmarks with limited impact on multimodal performance at modest inference-time overhead.

papers.title: SHIELD: Suppressing Hallucinations In LVLM Encoders via Bias and Vulnerability Defense
papers.contribution: Effectively mitigates object hallucinations across diverse benchmarks and LVLM families while achieving strong performance on general LVLM benchmarks.

papers.title: ScreenParse: Moving Beyond Sparse Grounding with Complete Screen Parsing Supervision
papers.contribution: ScreenVLM substantially outperforms larger foundation VLMs on dense parsing (0.592 vs 0.294 PageIoU) and shows strong transfer to public benchmarks.

papers.title: Adaptive Residual-Update Steering for Low-Overhead Hallucination Mitigation in Large Vision-Language Models
papers.contribution: RUDDER reduces CHAIR_S by 24.4% and CHAIR_i by 23.6% relative while maintaining >96.0% throughput across LLaVA, Idefics2, InstructBLIP, and Qwen2.5-VL.

papers.title: Bridging the Grounding Gap in VideoQA via Typed Memory for Language-based Belief-State Reasoning
papers.contribution: 82.4% on NExT-QA and 42.3% Acc@GQA on NExT-GQA; runs 2.6x faster than dense-frame methods with online adaptation.

papers.title: Capturing Gaze Shifts for Guidance: Cross-Modal Fusion Enhancement for VLM Hallucination Mitigation
papers.contribution: Mitigates VLM hallucination achieving up to 20.7% improvement over greedy decoding while maintaining general performance with low computational overhead.

papers.title: DeFacto: Counterfactual Thinking with Images for Enforcing Evidence-Grounded and Faithful Reasoning
papers.contribution: DeFacto substantially improves both answer accuracy and evidence-answer consistency over strong baselines on diverse benchmarks, with new DeFacto-1.5K benchmark for evaluating evidence-grounded consistency.

papers.title: Ego3S: Select, Strengthen, and Synchronize for Efficient Egocentric Reasoning
papers.contribution: Superior performance with only 26.5% training data and 46% computational reduction across five datasets.

papers.title: ExpAlign: Expectation-Guided Vision–Language Alignment for Open-Vocabulary Grounding
papers.contribution: ExpAlign achieves 36.2 AP_r on LVIS minival, outperforming comparable baselines on open-vocabulary detection and zero-shot instance segmentation while remaining lightweight and inference-efficient.

papers.title: Finding the Correct Visual Evidence Without Forgetting: Mitigating Hallucination in LVLMs via Inter-Layer Visual Attention Discrepancy
papers.contribution: The training-free, plug-and-play method consistently mitigates hallucinations across five different LVLMs and architectures.

papers.title: IRIS: Implicit Reward-Guided Internal Sifting for Mitigating Multimodal Hallucination
papers.contribution: IRIS achieves competitive hallucination mitigation on key benchmarks using only 5.7k samples without external feedback.

papers.title: Learning Attribute–Affordance Hierarchies in Hyperbolic Space for Open-Vocabulary 3D Object Affordance Grounding
papers.contribution: Achieve more accurate affordance localization through hierarchical attribute modeling and counterfactual training.

papers.title: Learning from Fine-Grained Visual Discrepancies: Mitigating Multimodal Hallucinations via In-Context Visual Contrastive Optimization
papers.contribution: IC-VCO achieves best overall performance on five benchmarks with hard negatives via semantic perturbations and better consistency between multi-image training and single-image inference.

papers.title: Learning to Decode Against Compositional Hallucination in Video Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.contribution: TriCD achieves over 10% average accuracy improvement on OmniVCHall across multiple video LLMs including Qwen3-VL and GPT-5.

papers.title: MACD: Model-Aware Contrastive Decoding via Counterfactual Data for Video-LLMs
papers.contribution: Reduces hallucination while maintaining task accuracy on EventHallusion, MVBench, Perception-test, and Video-MME; especially strong on small, occluded, or co-occurring objects.

papers.title: MM-Snowball: Evaluating and Mitigating Hallucination Snowballing in Multimodal Multi-Turn Dialogue
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on MM-Snowball, offering a path toward more reliable interactive AI.

papers.title: MedScope: Incentivizing "Think with Videos" for Clinical Reasoning via Coarse-to-Fine Tool Calling
papers.contribution: MedScope achieves state-of-the-art on video understanding benchmarks with predictions explicitly grounded in temporally localized visual evidence.

papers.title: Ophiuchus: Incentivizing Tool-augmented ''Think with Images'' for Joint Medical Segmentation, Understanding and Reasoning
papers.contribution: Outperforms both closed-source and open-source methods across diverse medical benchmarks including VQA, detection, and reasoning-based segmentation through three-stage training: cold-start SFT, self-reflection fine-tuning, and agentic tool reinforcement learni

papers.title: PostAlign: Multimodal Grounding as a Corrective Lens for MLLMs
papers.contribution: Significant improvements on POPE, HaloQuest, ReasonSeg, MME, and MMBench benchmarks with enhanced visual-textual alignment and reduced hallucinations.

papers.title: STVG-R1: Incentivizing Instance-Level Reasoning and Grounding in Videos via Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Achieved 20.9% improvement on m_IoU on HCSTVG-v2 over Qwen2.5-VL-7B and SOTA 47.3% J&F on zero-shot multi-object video segmentation.

papers.title: Spatio-Temporal LLM: Reasoning about Environments and Actions
papers.contribution: Both STLLM baselines outperform existing models on the REA dataset, demonstrating enhanced spatial understanding and temporal grounding.

papers.title: VideoSEAL: Mitigating Evidence Misalignment in Agentic Long Video Understanding by Decoupling Answer Authority
papers.contribution: Improves both answer accuracy and evidence alignment on LVBench and LongVideoBench; scales consistently with search budget increases and supports plug-and-play MLLM upgrades.
